There is a motion by Councilors Hollingsworth and Gardy, resolved that the report of the senior planner dated January 11, 2021, concerning rezoning application A1720Z be received and that Council rezone 352, 360 Northern Avenue from institutional zone and a Southwest portion, 36 by 36 meters of 31 Old Garden River Road from medium density residential zone with special exception to high density residential zone with a special exception to permit, in addition to the uses permitted in an R5 zone, a seven-story apartment building and a place of worship subject to the following special provisions. Reduce the required east interior side yard setback from 10.21 meters to zero meters to accommodate a link between the proposed new building and the existing CARA-1 apartment building. Reduce required parking from 89 spaces to 72 spaces inclusive of six barrier-free spaces for both the proposed residential and place of worship uses. Reduce required landscape open space from 33% to 29%. Permit required parking to be located in a required front and exterior side yard. Waive the need to provide a dedicated loading space as required by section six of zoning by-law 2005-150 and that the legal department be requested to prepare the necessary by-laws to effect the same. Councilor, council, I should say for the applicant has been admitted in from the waiting room and I believe the consultant as well.

speaker: donmcconnell
text: Okay, so I'll start with you, Mr. McConnell. Thank you, Mr. Mayor. This is the Holy Trinity Church. It's an Anglican church on the corner of Northern Avenue, Great Northern Road and Old Garden River Road. The proposal is to demolish the church as well as the four townhouse units that are the most westerly units in order to construct a new seven-story, 58-unit apartment building. Of those 58 units, 20 of them, I was going to say meet the provincial definition, but actually they exceed the provincial definition of affordable housing and they will be affordable. It is a very good development. We have not heard from the abutting neighbors at all. It is recommended for approval. Mr. Spadafora is the solicitor for the applicant and I see he is on the line tonight along with several of the consultants from SHS Consulting, which is the consulting firm that's housing, that is assisting carer community with this development. I'd be happy to answer your questions. I don't know if Mr. Spadafora has opening comments or not.

speaker: provenzano
text: Mr. Spadafora, did you want to speak to this matter? Does the applicant want to speak to this matter?

speaker: carlospadafora
text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mayor and to council. I know it's January the 11th and I know we're deep in deeper into the new year. So I'll start off by wishing everybody a happy new year. And hopefully this one's a little different than last year. Anyways, that said, this is, I think Mr. McConnell's report and the planning report is pretty straightforward. This is, and I'm here, I know SHS has been identified, but Mr. Starr, Mylene Vincent, who's probably, who I understand may be attending on another matter and Andrew Verana are also there. They're part of the planning team that also includes MGP for this application. And the applicant Carrick Community Corporation is one that I'm sure many of you are already familiar with and the work they've done and the types of developments that they have done in and around this area. And I think that this is one that speaks very much to the evolution of the property. It is a little different than some of the other projects or some of the other complexes that are there with Carrick Community Corporation. This is one as Mr. McConnell's identified as an affordable housing or an affordable rent type of project different than rent that's geared to income. I think it's, it underlines the fact that this has been, I wanted to underline the fact that this has been a good working relationship between city staff, the applicant, it's a planning team and the opportunity to speak with one of the particular councilors with regards to this, this opportunity council Shoemaker. And I think that basically this is something that makes sense and would perhaps compliment in many ways the very important intersection that is Gray Northern Road, Northern Avenue and Old Garden River Road. I will not get into and dive into the details that are already covered off from the council report. But I think that given the type of care, the type of entity that Carrick Community Corporation is, the extension of this project and development, I think that it has hit all of the key elements of these types of developments that we see complimenting and growing throughout the community. And I think it speaks volumes in that sense. And one final thing to underline is that part of this request for severance is also geared towards the funding formula that the developer and the applicant is obviously looking for as part of the process where this is a standalone piece of property. I'll hold my comments to there.

speaker: provenzano
text: Okay, thank you for those Mr. Spadafora. Now clerk, do we have anybody that asked to register to speak in opposition to the application? We have none. A council, you've heard from planning and you've heard from the applicant. There's no one registered to speak in opposition to it. You have any questions? Councilor Basile and then Councilor Hollingsworth.

speaker: vez
text: Thank you. Through you, Mr. Mayor to Mr. McConnell. Mr. McConnell, do you know how many barrier free units there are going to be in the new facility?

speaker: donmcconnell
text: Through you, Mr. Mayor to Councilor Bresow-Allen. We have had discussions with the applicant on that matter. Under the Ontario building code, they're required to have 15 units or sorry, 15% of the units are barrier free. They are planning on having 30% of the units as barrier free.

speaker: rvezeau
text: That's wonderful.

speaker: vez
text: And I just wanna say a comment that on behalf of the Accessibility Committee, and I know Diane did a report. This is a great extension to what CARE Community does. And I'm really happy to approve this project. And I think it will be a great benefit for our community in terms of both access to adequate housing for people that have barriers, but as well in terms of affordability. So thanks very much for everyone that put work into this. Nothing else.

speaker: provenzano
text: Okay, Councilor Hollingsworth.

speaker: hollingsworth
text: Thank you. Through you, Your Worship to Mr. McConnell. Again, just reiterate how many units are, so how many units in each of the four townhouses being built?

speaker: donmcconnell
text: I'm sorry, Mr. Mayor, I didn't quite catch the question.

speaker: provenzano
text: I think perhaps Councilor Hollingsworth might've misunderstood earlier your comment you made about the townhouses, which are being approved to build the building. So if you could just explain, I think the essence of the question is how many units are being constructed in total?

speaker: donmcconnell
text: Okay, thank you, Mr. Mayor. In order to make room for the new building, they will be removing the church and four townhouse units. That gives them a large block of land. On that block of land will be the new 58 unit building. So at the end of the day, there'll be a net gain of 54 units.

speaker: hollingsworth
text: Okay, and I'm under the impression that they're gonna comprise be different variations like one bedroom, two bedrooms. Can you comment on that?

speaker: donmcconnell
text: Yes, it's a mixture of one and two bedroom units. The entire building is either one or two bedrooms, yes.

speaker: hollingsworth
text: Okay, and for those that may not be familiar with CARA, can you just give us a very high level overview of CARA, what other projects they may have done elsewhere outside of our community?

speaker: donmcconnell
text: I'm not sure if CARA has done other projects outside our community. Certainly, SHS Consulting has worked with nonprofit housing all over the province. But as far as CARA having any projects outside our community, I don't believe so. That was an organization that was originally affiliated with the Anglican Church here locally. Mr. Spadafore, did you have something else you wanted to add to that?

speaker: carlospadafora
text: Yes, I guess it's just for a point of clarification. Thank you very much. When I talk about CARA community and the projects and their presence, I do mean here within the city. And actually, this particular site is next to some of the other buildings and properties that they have in the same area there that when you head down Old Garden River Road and also fronting on Northern Avenue where those townhouse complexes are. So, I mean, they have been in the business if I can call it that, of multi-unit residential projects such as this one.

speaker: hollingsworth
text: Okay, and one last question. Again, when are you or are they hoping to have these, what's the basically timeline when these will be constructed, 2021 and so forth?

speaker: donmcconnell
text: Mr. Mayor, perhaps either Mr. Spadafore or Mr. Starr could answer that for us.

speaker: carlospadafora
text: I will also ask Mr. Starr to weigh in on this, but I would start by suggesting that if timelines were to prevail as planned, it would be, I guess, in the fall. Mr. Starr.

speaker: edstarr
text: Yes, so with the approval of this zoning, this makes us eligible to apply for project funding from CMHC. They have a program called the co-investment fund and it takes them, we'll be able to move ahead if we're approved today in the, I guess we have the appeal period. We'll be able to move ahead with our application and it takes them about four or five months to review the application. We've already received some preliminary seed funding. So there's a good likelihood that we would be approved by the latter part of the year. And then once the funding is approved, we just have to tender it out and start construction. It's likely that we wouldn't get a shovel in the ground until the new year, given the length of time, all the approvals take, et cetera, not the city approvals, the funding from the federal government. So, but that does enable us to come through with the affordable rents.

speaker: hollingsworth
text: Great, wonderful project. So I don't think you need best of luck because you have all the experience, but this is very good for our community. Thank you.

speaker: provenzano
text: We've got a bit of a list. I have Councilor Bruni, then Dufour, then Shoemaker.

speaker: marchybruni
text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. Excellent project to come forward. Just a couple of questions I have, and I believe Mr. McConnell might be able to answer them. Regarding the 89 spaces reduced to 72, if the worship space is for 80 people, plus all the apartments, is the parking spaces sufficient?

speaker: donmcconnell
text: Through you, Mr. Mayor to Councilor Bruni, yes. There's really two considerations when we looked at the parking. One is most of the congregation currently resides in CARA now. They have a very small congregation that comes from outside the immediate area. And those people will, there'll be a physical connection between the two buildings. Those people will simply walk. If there is, if for some reason there's a special occasion or whatever, and parking does become a problem, CARA has a considerable amount of parking right in the area. The reduction in spaces is just for this building. They do meet the bylaw requirements for the other three buildings, the other three properties that they own that are but this property. So I don't envision parking being a problem at all.

speaker: marchybruni
text: So the only entrance will be on Northern Avenue. There won't be any other entrance, or I guess the entrance and exit is only on Northern Avenue on this project now.

speaker: donmcconnell
text: We did look at the possibility of having entrances onto Old Garden River Road as well, because the parking lots do connect. So there will be more than one access into and out of the parking lot, the parking area.

speaker: marchybruni
text: Right, okay. Regarding the loading space, I know most apartment buildings have a loading space for smaller transports to drop off items. So it was your, well, it was the recommendation from your department not to provide one, or you need to provide one.

speaker: donmcconnell
text: Through you, Mayor Parmigiano to Councillor Bruni. Actually, the original drawings did show a loading space, and there will be space there for a large transport to load and unload. The difficulty is with the CMHC financing, they had to sever the properties. So what we ended up with is half of a loading space that's on the old property, and half of the loading space that's on the new property. But for all intents and purposes, yes, there will be a loading space there, and we'll identify that as part of our site plan agreement.

speaker: marchybruni
text: And my final question is regarding the three meter road widening along Northern Avenue that was just re-asphalted in the summer. Who picks up that cost? Is that the city cost or the developer's cost?

speaker: donmcconnell
text: Through you, Mr. Mayor to Councillor Bruni, that's the cost of the developer. He will pay for the survey and the cost of transferring that to the municipality.

speaker: marchybruni
text: And the widening of it, who, like the material and all that, is that from the developer, he pays for it?

speaker: donmcconnell
text: Through you again, Mr. Mayor, I don't think there's any immediate plans to widen the road, but when the road is widened, that will be at the city's cost. The applicant is only responsible for the property costs and having that property transferred to the city. Any infrastructure improvements would be a municipal cost.

speaker: marchybruni
text: But in the reports, there's a three meter road widening along Northern Avenue will be needed.

speaker: donmcconnell
text: Yes.

speaker: marchybruni
text: Because of this, correct?

speaker: donmcconnell
text: Because of the development? No, it's just because of the traffic volumes that are there now. This development by itself will not generate sufficient traffic to widen Northern Avenue further. speaker: marchybruni
text: Okay, thank you.

speaker: provenzano
text: Okay, so Council Dunford and Councilor Schoenmaker.

speaker: dufour
text: Thanks, Mr. Mayor.

speaker: dufo
text: I believe this, I'm not sure if this question

speaker: dufour
text: would go to Mr. McConnell or to Mr. Starr, but in reviewing the report,

speaker: dufo
text: it talks about the affordability question of, I believe, 34% of the rents. My question is, will the affordable rent units be affordable to low or moderate income households or both? It states the provincial policy statement shows low and moderate. And then I couldn't find any more information about that after that in the report.

speaker: provenzano
text: Mr. Starr, are you able to answer that question?

speaker: edstarr
text: Yes. So under the CMHC co-investment program, it's a requirement that at least 30% of the units must be 20% below average market rent. So CMHC publishes a survey of average market rents in the community, and we must ensure that at least 30% of the units are below that level. We are also allowed to apply to the service manager to see if they also have any additional, what they call rent supplement units or shelter allowance units to bring the rents down further. But the likelihood is that we'll be able to achieve about 20% below average market rent, given the nature of the funding formula in this program.

speaker: dufo
text: Great, thanks, Mr. Starr. So is the number of affordable units in the building then going to be 20% or 34%?

speaker: edstarr
text: I think we're at 34% according to our latest calculations. It must be at least 30% in order to qualify for the funding.

speaker: dufo
text: Okay, and of that 30%, is there a certain portion that's low and a certain portion that's moderate?

speaker: edstarr
text: Well, they give us basically some flexibility there, but according to the financial calculations, we'll be hard pressed to do any better than 20% below the market rent. The programs that they have these days simply do not go any deeper than that, unless we do get assistance from the service manager to, as I said, to get some rent supplement units or that sort of thing, which we'll certainly pursue. But the baseline is that 30% of the units will be 20% below CMHC market rent.

speaker: dufo
text: Okay, I'm sorry, Mr. Starr, I think I misunderstood you before. That was my question, wasn't clarifying. You're saying 20% below the income threshold, and I was asking questions about the percentage of units available to be affordable, would be 34% and the amount of affordability would be 20% below the relative income thresholds.

speaker: edstarr
text: That's right.

speaker: dufour
text: Okay, and just to further clarify

speaker: dufo
text: that the supplements are coming from the federal CMHC co-investment fund at this time?

speaker: edstarr
text: Yes, that's right. It's all federal money. And the way that program works is there is no specific allocation for any one city or community. It goes on a case-by-case basis. So if Farah weren't applying for these funds and nobody else was applying from Sault Ste. Marie, they would simply go to some other location. So it's not like they said, Sault Ste. Marie is going to get so many units and then we'll try and find some projects. It's on the initiative of Cara that these federal funds will come into the city of Sault Ste. Marie. So that's the way this program works.

speaker: dufo
text: Understood, and my final question is, have you approached the service manager to inquire about other rent subs?

speaker: edstarr
text: Yes, so we have, and they've invited us to, once our co-investment application is approved to apply and they're going to do their best to see if they have some funds kicking around from some of their current programs. It's possible. I do expect we'll likely get maybe a small amount that can come in that much reduced rents, which would be the rent supplements that are 30% of income. So if somebody is on, let's say, Ontario disability, it would be like about 497 a month is what they would pay under those programs. So that's what we're going to aim for as much as they have available.

text: Excellent, well, thank you all very much

speaker: dufo
text: and thank you to the Cara Community Corporation. It's wonderful to see other folks also building affordable housing in Sault Ste. Marie. Thanks very much, Mr. Bichard.
